definitions.gloss: to distract oneself; to take one's mind off something
definitions.explanation: To do something in order to divert one's attention from worry, sadness, boredom, or discomfort.

examples.japanese: ⟦{散歩|さんぽ}→散歩：02885_sanpo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧{気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らす。
examples.english: I take a walk to take my mind off things.

examples.japanese: ⟦{音楽|おんがく}→音楽：00661_ongaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聴|き}いて→聴く：30010_kiku⟧{気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らした。
examples.english: I listened to music to distract myself.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{気|き}になる→気になる：03027_kininaru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧{気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らすことにした。
examples.english: I'm anxious about the exam results, but I decided to cook to take my mind off it.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
This is a set phrase using {紛|まぎ}らす (to divert, to distract). The verb {紛|まぎ}らす conjugates as a godan verb: {紛|まぎ}らさない / {紛|まぎ}らして / {紛|まぎ}らした.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らす⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (in order to distract oneself)
- {気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らす⟦{方法|ほうほう}→方法：03621_houhou⟧ (a way to take one's mind off things)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{散|ち}らす→散らす：02288_chirasu⟧ means to distract in a more general sense (including unwanted distractions). ⟦{気晴|きば}らし→気晴らし：16699_kibarashi⟧ (diversion, pastime) is the noun form of the same concept.
